policy.reason: Kaggle benchmark runs must spend GPU time evaluating models, not compiling native runtimes.
policy.onMissingCompatibleBinary: record runtime_unqualified and stop; do not invoke cmake, ninja, make, cargo, nvcc, setup.py build, pip source distributions, or flash-attn source compilation
policy.pipPolicy: use --only-binary=:all: for native packages; never use --no-binary or --no-build-isolation to force a source build
policy.sourceBuildException: allowed only as a separately authorized runtime-development experiment; never as the canonical Issue #25 benchmark path
policy.dependencyClosureReason: Issue #41: a pinned vLLM wheel still imports differently as Kaggle's mutable global torch/torchvision/transformers packages change. The complete serving environment is part of the runtime identity, so a Python wheel artifact may only be installed when every runtime-critical dependency is version+hash bound in a reviewed lock.
policy.isolationReason: Issue #41: the canonical path must not import or mutate arbitrary Kaggle global site-packages. Python wheel artifacts install into a dedicated virtual environment created under --dest and every runtime probe runs with that interpreter under isolated mode.
policy.onDependencyLockPending: record runtime_unqualified with classification dependency_lock_pending and stop; do not fall back to unpinned pip resolution
policy.onInstalledPackageDrift: record runtime_unqualified and stop; do not silently upgrade, downgrade, or reinstall to make an import pass

artifacts.notes: Official vLLM release wheel. Driver/runtime compatibility must be proven by Kaggle preflight/import smoke; do not rebuild if incompatible.
Official vendor prebuilt; preferred compatibility probe when CUDA 12.4 is safer for the Kaggle driver.
Official vendor prebuilt already exercised successfully on Kaggle glibc 2.35 in the Bonsai 27B qualification run.

dependencyLockSchema.description: Machine-readable freeze of the runtime-critical Python dependency closure for one python_wheel artifact. Produced on the real Kaggle image, reviewed, then committed together with its sha256 in environments[].dependencyLock.
rules: every package has exactly one version and at least one sha256 of an upstream wheel actually installed by pip
optional=true is permitted only for candidate-specific extras such as quantization backends; the canonical default profile requires optional=false
resolutionReport carries the sha256 of the machine-readable `pip install --report` capture that produced these pins
evidenceGaps must be empty before dependencyLock.state may be set to locked

resolutionReportSchema.description: Verbatim capture of `pip install --report` JSON plus the installer's captured stdout/stderr, retained next to the runtime receipt.

python.note: stable-ABI (cp38-abi3) build, so one wheel covers CPython 3.10-3.14; verified from the pinned wheel's own METADATA and WHEEL members

evidenceGaps: NOT a promotion lock. kaggle-runtime-locks/vllm-0.30.0-cu129-linux-x86_64.candidate-lock.json was produced by resolving this exact cu129 wheel with pip install --dry-run --report on a macOS arm64 host (python3.12 pip 26.1) using explicit --platform manylinux_2_17/2_28/2_31_x86_64, manylinux2014_x86_64, linux_x86_64 and --python-version 3.11 --abi cp311 --abi abi3. That resolution completed with 180 packages, all 180 hash-bound (178 hashes straight from the pip report; torchvision and Jinja2 hashed locally because the pytorch index publishes those two without a #sha256 fragment).

The candidate lock is NOT promotion evidence: it was resolved for CPython 3.11 only. The Kaggle base image Python minor version is still unpinned in this repository, and torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchvision 0.28.0+cu129 and torchaudio 2.11.0+cu129 publish a DIFFERENT wheel per CPython tag (cp310..cp315), so the hashes recorded here are only valid for a cp311 image. Read python.version from the real Kaggle preflight receipt before locking.

torchvision 0.28.0+cu129 wheel hashes were computed locally by downloading each exact URL (cp310..cp314 x86_64) and hashing it; the cu129 index publishes a data-dist-info-metadata hash for torchvision, which is a different file and must not be used as a wheel hash. Verify these against the target image resolution before promotion.

The cu129 wheel requires llguidance>=1.7.0,<1.8.0, whose 1.7.x releases publish ONLY cp39-abi3 manylinux_2_31+ (or per-CPython CPython-version-specific wheels); the cp311 dry-run had to add --abi abi3 and --platform manylinux_2_31_x86_64 to resolve it. A cp310 image may fail to resolve llguidance from binary wheels alone, which would be a genuine runtime_unqualified rather than a source-build trigger.

flashinfer-cubin 0.6.18.post1 is not on PyPI (it exists only at https://flashinfer.ai/whl/) and did not appear in the dry-run resolution; whether the frozen runtime needs it remains undecided from the wheel metadata alone.

torchaudio 2.11.0 declares NO torch dependency even though its C extension links libtorch internals, so torchaudio/torch skew is only detectable by import inside the venv. No target-image import smoke has run, so this closure is unproven on T4.

The dry-run resolution also surfaced nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu12 AND nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13 together, which is consistent with the cu129 wheel metadata carrying both; whether both are needed is unverified and any installed table must be compared against this closure on the target image.

candidateLock.note: Off-image candidate closure only. Bound into the registry by sha256 so it cannot be edited silently, but NOT usable for installation: the install gate reads dependencyLock.state and refuses anything but 'locked'. Promote only by re-resolving on the real Kaggle image and committing the closure as a locked lock with its own sha256.

artifactVerification.claim: the pinned vllm-0.30.0+cu129-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl exists upstream and its digest matches the registry pin
artifactVerification.caveat: digest restated from GitHub's published asset digest; the 545 MB wheel body was not re-hashed locally

metadataSources: vllm-0.30.0+cu129.dist-info/METADATA extracted from the pinned release wheel via HTTP range requests

torchStack.torch: ==2.13.0 (resolves to torch-2.13.0+cu129 from the cu129 index)
torchStack.torchvision: ==0.28.0 (Requires-Dist: torch (==2.13.0), so pip enforces the pairing)
torchStack.torchaudio: ==2.11.0 (declares no torch dependency; skew only shows up at import)
torchStack.warning: plain PyPI torch==2.13.0 is the CUDA 13 build (cuda-toolkit 13.0.3, nvidia-*-cu13); the lock MUST come from the cu129 index or the whole CUDA runtime silently moves from 12.9 to 13.0.

upstreamEvidence.notInClosureNote: None of these appear in the cu129 wheel's Requires-Dist. vLLM 0.30.0 reaches FlashAttention/FlashInfer through its own bundled kernels plus flashinfer-python, not through xformers. They must not be pinned unless a specific candidate actually imports them.

importSmoke.reason: CUDA tag, driver version, and visible compute capability decide T4 qualification
Issue #41 cites real upstream import-time torch/torchvision operator mismatches; a compiled-op call catches ABI skew that a bare import misses
tokenizer/config stack is version-bound in the lock
proves the pinned wheel is importable from the isolated venv and not a stale global package
exercises console-script entrypoint imports before any multi-GB model download

cuda.onUnavailable: record runtime_unqualified with classification environment_cuda_unavailable; a successful import alone never qualifies a candidate

bitsandbytes.reason: quantization-only dependency; required only by candidates that select this profile
